body:
If the words I couldn’t speak could scream,

they would.



All the things I thought I understood,

how easily I wore certainty,

how quietly it left me.



I believed you would stay.

That you would know

when to reach for me.



I shouted

or maybe I didn’t.



The words stayed lodged somewhere

between breath and death,

and your absence learned

how to echo.



Morning comes anyway.

Coffee going cold in my hands,

your scent - imagined or remembered -

lingers longer than it should.



I keep trying to live on what’s left:

fragments, habits,

the soft repetition of your name

in rooms that don’t answer.



Everything turns the same color

blue.

then bluer.

then some shade without a name.



Night arrives without asking.

I still wait for it,

that small, ordinary kindness:

good night.



But you were never there

to say it.



And I am left

with all this silence

and nowhere

to place it.
